articles.title: Tom Brady’s $32.5 million home sale record faces a new challenge from a $34 million Brookline mansion
articles.summary: A luxury mansion in Brookline, Massachusetts, is making a bold bid to claim the town’s most expensive home sale record.
articles.body: A luxury mansion in Brookline, Massachusetts, is making a bold bid to claim the town’s most expensive home sale record. Listed for $34 million, the sprawling estate near Brookline Reservoir could surpass the reported $32.5 million sale of Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen’s former home. With seven bedrooms, a private tennis court and sweeping views of Boston, the property offers a glimpse into New England’s elite real estate market. However, its ambitious asking price comes as local home sales slow, leaving a big question: will a buyer pay enough to rewrite Brookline’s property history?Inside the $34 million Brookline mansion challenging Tom Brady’s recordLocated at 55 Singletree Road, the hilltop estate covers 19,138 square feet on 2.06 acres. Built in 2015 by luxury homebuilder Thoughtforms, the residence combines generous living space with features designed for privacy and leisure.The property includes seven bedrooms, 16 bathrooms, five fireplaces, a swimming pool, a private tennis court and a fitness centre. A rooftop terrace also offers views of the Boston skyline, adding another attraction to the expansive home.The estate’s price stands out even in one of Massachusetts’ wealthiest communities. According to records cited in local reporting, Brookline assessed the property at $18,959,800 in 2025. Its annual property tax bill reached $187,133, a substantial cost even for buyers shopping in the luxury market.The land itself has a long history. Public records show that the parcel last sold in 1993 for just over $1 million. The current owner, an LLC linked to a partner at a Manhattan estate-planning firm, took out a $9.1 million mortgage in 2015.The Sarkis Team at Douglas Elliman Real Estate is handling the listing. The brokers have experience with high-value properties in the area, including the nearby estate of former Reebok founder Paul Fireman, which sold for $23 million in 2020.How Tom Brady’s former Brookline mansion set the benchmarkTom Brady and Gisele Bündchen’s former Brookline estate remains a major reference point for the new listing. The couple bought a five-acre parcel at 112 Woodland Road from Pine Manor College for $4.5 million in 2013 before building a custom mansion designed by architect Richard Landry.The 12,112-square-foot home initially went on the market for $39.5 million in 2019. After price reductions and a brief withdrawal, it eventually sold for a reported $32.5 million in 2021.The new $34 million listing aims to exceed that figure, although the asking price does not guarantee a record-breaking sale.Brookline’s wider housing market could also complicate the seller’s ambitions. Data from MLS PIN cited by the Brookline Record showed that the town recorded 25 home sales in September, down 44% from 45 sales a year earlier. The median time properties spent on the market also doubled to 71 days.Still, exceptional estates often attract a different pool of buyers from ordinary homes. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million Six Flags investment faces new concerns as Citizens slashes stock target by $10
articles.summary: Six Flags is facing fresh pressure on Wall Street, and the latest warning comes at a difficult time for the amusement park giant.
articles.body: Six Flags is facing fresh pressure on Wall Street, and the latest warning comes at a difficult time for the amusement park giant. Citizens has sharply reduced its price target for the company after weaker visitor numbers raised concerns about its financial outlook. The development also puts the spotlight on Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end who serves as a Six Flags ambassador and investor. With the company dealing with declining attendance, financial strain and the fallout from a fatal incident at one of its parks, investors will be watching closely to see whether new leadership can restore confidence and bring visitors back.Citizens cuts Six Flags stock price target after attendance declinesCitizens lowered its price target for Six Flags Entertainment (NYSE: FUN) from $24 to $14, although it maintained a Market Outperform rating. The revised target reflects growing concerns about the company's performance during the third quarter, traditionally one of its most important periods.Six Flags' same-store attendance is estimated to have fallen 2% in the third quarter of 2026. That contrasts with market expectations for a 0.2% increase, suggesting the company struggled to attract as many visitors as analysts had anticipated.The stock was trading at $7.07 in the report, close to its 52-week low of $6.96. Shares had also fallen 17% over the previous seven days, while the company's market capitalisation stood at approximately $723 million.The financial picture adds to the pressure. Six Flags reported second-quarter revenue of $865 million, 7% below consensus expectations, despite a 2% year-over-year increase in same-store revenue. Other analysts have also lowered their targets, citing weaker revenue trends, weather-related disruptions and rising leverage.Citizens further reduced its fourth-quarter 2026 EBITDA estimate by 10% following a fatal incident at one of the company's parks in October. The company must now manage the operational fallout while working to rebuild public confidence.Travis Kelce’s Six Flags investment faces a crucial periodKelce's connection with Six Flags gives the company's latest challenges an added layer of interest. As both an ambassador and investor, the NFL star has a commercial relationship with a brand that now needs to strengthen its reputation and improve its financial performance.However, the available report does not disclose the size of Kelce's investment or indicate whether the latest stock decline has affected his personal holdings. His involvement should not be taken as evidence of any direct financial loss.Six Flags has also welcomed a new CEO and CFO within the past year. Citizens expects management to prioritise customer confidence and operational improvements as the business moves through its slower season.There is still a potential path to recovery. Citizens does not expect the October incident to have a material effect on results during spring 2027, when attendance typically improves. The coming months will test whether Six Flags can turn that seasonal opportunity into sustained growth.For Kelce and other investors, the key question is whether the company can bring visitors back, stabilise its finances and regain market confidence. articles.title: Jay-Z isn’t performing at Super Bowl LXI? Roger Goodell breaks silence on halftime show rumors
articles.summary: The race to headline Super Bowl LXI has already sparked a wave of speculation, with Jay-Z emerging as one of the biggest names in the conversation.
articles.body: The race to headline Super Bowl LXI has already sparked a wave of speculation, with Jay-Z emerging as one of the biggest names in the conversation. The hip-hop icon has helped shape the NFL’s halftime entertainment since his company, Roc Nation, partnered with the league in 2019. Now, a report suggesting that he selected himself for the upcoming show has put the spotlight on his unusual position in the selection process. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell has finally addressed the growing buzz, but his response has stopped short of confirming or denying Jay-Z’s involvement.Roger Goodell responds to Jay-Z Super Bowl LXI halftime show rumorsSpeaking at a news conference on Wednesday, Goodell faced questions about reports that Jay-Z could headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show. Rather than confirm the speculation, the NFL commissioner stressed that the league had not made an official announcement.“I am not aware of a leak. “I’ve been in the committee meetings. So I’m not sure it’s a leak. We haven’t announced anything. Until we do, we won’t make any comment on that.”His comments followed a report from Puck claiming that Jay-Z had selected himself to perform at the event, despite his role in helping the NFL choose its halftime headliners. The report also linked Miley Cyrus and Justin Bieber to the potential lineup, although neither artist has received official confirmation.Jay-Z, 56, has never headlined the Super Bowl halftime show himself. Since Roc Nation began working with the NFL in 2019, the partnership has helped bring major artists such as Rihanna, Usher, Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny to the stage.That history makes the latest speculation particularly interesting. Jay-Z has considerable influence over the show's production, but whether he intends to take centre stage remains unknown.Jay-Z’s Super Bowl LXI rumors grow ahead of the 2027 gameJay-Z's possible appearance would mark a new chapter in his relationship with the NFL. The rapper is also celebrating major milestones in his music career through his Jay-Z 30 Tour, which marks 30 years since Reasonable Doubt and 25 years since The Blueprint. The tour is his first major run of shows since 2018, when he toured with Beyoncé on the On the Run II tour.However, the league has a history of keeping its halftime plans under wraps. Before Super Bowl LX, Taylor Swift was linked to the show in several reports, but Bad Bunny ultimately headlined the performance in Santa Clara. He became the first Latino artist to headline the show solo and the first to perform entirely in Spanish, with Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin joining him on stage.Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. With no headliner confirmed, speculation about Jay-Z, Cyrus and Bieber is likely to continue.For now, Goodell's remarks offer no final answer. articles.title: NBA’s Irving praises Al-Shaair’s ‘selfless act’ after Hind Rajab fine paid
articles.summary: Kyrie Irving explains paying fine and praises Azeez Al-Shaair for continuously honouring slain Palestinian children.
articles.body:
NBA star Kyrie Irving has opened up about his decision to pay a fine for American football player Azeez Al-Shaair, who was penalised in September for wearing the name of Hind Rajab , a Palestinian girl killed by Israeli forces in Gaza.

“Azeez is a friend of mine,” Irving told reporters, after suffering an opening night 128-110 defeat with Dallas Mavericks in the match against Houston Rockets late on Wednesday.

“He’s a brother that I consider in this revolution this generation is building. It’s a selfless act when you can show up for others who don’t necessarily have a voice for themselves,” said Irving, who has been vocal in his support for Palestine.

Al-Shaair has used his social media accounts and his eyeblack, a tape worn by athletes to reduce glare, to bring attention to the killings of Palestinians in the three years of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

The Black American Muslim player began his current NFL season by wearing Rajab’s name on September 13. The five-year-old girl was killed in Gaza after Israeli soldiers opened fire on her family’s stranded car on January 29, 2024.

For that, Al-Shaair was handed a fine of $11,941 by the National Football League (NFL). Shortly after the fine was announced by an NFL reporter on X, Irving responded to the tweet by saying he would “take care” of it.

“I think we assume that most of us know what’s happening around the world globally,” Irving said on Wednesday. “There are a lot of innocent people who have lost their lives, children especially.

“Us here in America, we get the luxury of going to bed at night in our nice bedrooms, things paid for, but when our tax dollars are going towards other things that we don’t necessarily agree with, then you have to stand up.

“I think small instances of revolutionary acts like wearing people’s names or wearing a child’s name like Hind Rajab on your face and taking a fine and stepping up to the plate, it just shows how much you’re a selfless person, how much you’re willing to sacrifice,” Irving said.

“This mission is bigger than me and Azeez and we know that, but our strength and solidarity and how connected we are and how united we are in our efforts.”

Al-Shaair honours Palestinian children for fifth straight week

Despite being fined and reportedly threatened with removal from games, Al-Shaair has remained undeterred.

When asked, he brushed off the fine regarding Rajab, saying: “It’s bigger to me; what’s a life worth? Is a life worth $11,000? No, I think it’s priceless.”

He has continued to raise awareness about the slain children by wearing a name, or combination of names, every Sunday.

After honouring Rajab, Al-Shaair took the field against the Cincinnati Bengals wearing the name of Wafa Akila , an eight-year-old who was killed along with her father in an Israeli attack in western Gaza as they were making their way home.

In Week 3 against the Indianapolis Colts, Al-Shaair’s eye black had the names of sisters Lana and Bana Ahmad on it. The 12- and eight-year-old girls were killed along with their family in an Israeli air attack in September.

The Houston Texans’ linebacker then wore the name of Amal Abu Khater, 10, who died from gunshot wounds after Israeli forces fired on her in Khan Younis in August.

Al-Shaair’s latest tribute was to slain Palestinian toddler Maryam Ghanem, a two-and-a-half-year-old girl in Gaza who was forced to watch her mother burn alive after an Israeli strike hit their home in the Remal neighbourhood of Gaza City earlier this month.

articles.title: Bold Predictions for Cleveland Browns at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline is less than three weeks away, which means it's decision time for teams around the league.
articles.body:
The Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline is less than three weeks away, which means it's decision time for teams around the league.

It isn't often that the Browns are considered buyers at the trade deadline, but their place in the standings puts them in that position. Andrew Berry could look at this start as the team's best opportunity to compete in a long time and decide to get aggressive.

At the same time, the Browns have a few tradeable assets who could bring back some trade capital or cap relief over the next few seasons.

Here are a few bold predictions as the deadline approaches over the next few weeks.

The Browns might be in a good position at 4-2, but Jerry Jeudy has been a tough watch at times this season. The veteran receiver has been downright MIA on more than one occasion this year.

His early struggles made him a popular trade candidate. Jeudy had just two catches over the first three games and was clearly passed up by Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion.

The trade speculation got to the point where it was reported that the Browns wanted a third- or fourth-round pick for the veteran receiver.

The problem is that Jeudy has shown his worth to the Browns over the last few weeks. His production might not live up to his contract, but he had four catches for 69 yards in the win over the Ravens including the key catch that set up the game-winning field goal.

The reality is that Jeudy is the best option outside of Concepcion and Boston on the roster. Isaiah Bond and Tylan Wallace have both had opportunities to take over the role and no one has stepped up.

Even if the Browns' 4-2 record isn't enough to make them a buyer, the receiver room just isn't deep enough to trade a veteran of Jeudy's ability.

Jerry Jeudy has come up a lot in trade rumors and speculation. Shedeur Sanders is the other name that always comes up.

While it's hard to see them dealing Jeudy when he's actually carved out a role over the last few weeks, the same can't be said for Sanders.

Early in the season, it seemed Sanders was in a legitimate quarterback competition. Deshaun Watson got the nod, but if things went off the rails, it wasn't hard to see them going to Sanders to start.

At 4-2 with Watson playing well enough for the Browns to win games, that seems less likely. Meanwhile, Sanders hired an agent for the first time in his NFL career.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported, based on his discussions with people around the league and Browns officials, it would be a surprise if Sanders were moved prior to the trade deadline.

There are surprises at the deadline all the time, though.

The Browns postponed a decision on their four-quarterback situation by placing Dillon Gabriel on injured reserve earlier in the year. However, they opened his 21-day practice window on October 6, meaning they must either activate him or leave him on injured reserve for the rest of the season.

Keeping Sanders, Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green might be feasible for a week if they need to facilitate a deal, but having four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster is not ideal.

If the Browns can flip Sanders for a draft pick, it would make sense to do so in the coming weeks. They aren't benching Watson soon and they'll need to reevalute the position next season.

One of the most underrated needs on the roster right now is a blocking tight end. In an offseason where much of the league was trying to add at the position and to run 13 personnel (one running back, three tight ends), the Browns currently have just two on the active roster.

Harold Fannin has been underwhelming in the receiving game. He has just 166 yards on 19 receptions on the season thus far, but it's not really his fault. He's getting open on routes, but he's not getting targeted as often and he's had to play in-line tight end more often.

The Browns are using 11 personnel at the fourth-highest rate in the league, leaving only one tight end on the field in those sets. Adding a dependable blocking tight end could give Cleveland more flexibility in how it deploys Fannin.

He's getting open . His abilities as a receiver haven't suddenly disappeared. However, Blake Whiteheart doesn't stand out as a blocker so the Browns have preferred their three-receiver sets.

The solution could come at the trade deadline. Trades for tight ends aren't common, but the cost has typically been a Day 3 pick. Nick Vannett, Brevin Jordan and Tyler Conklin are all veterans with expiring contracts and a low snap count for their current team.

The Browns are 28th in the league in time with a lead , so it's definitely fair to say they are a little more flawed than your average 4-2 team.

Yet, they continue to find ways to win. It hasn't been pretty, but they have AFC North wins over the Steelers and Ravens. Both could wind up being important down the stretch when the playoff picture takes shape.

The reality is that the Browns are setting themselves up for a run at the postseason, even if it's ahead of their timeline as an organization.

The defense is for real. The defensive front continues to generate pressure on the quarterback in the post-Myles Garrett era. The Browns are second in the league in sacks and are seventh in scoring defense.

The schedule is going to continue to give the Browns a chance to overachieve. They have four games until the bye week and the only team with a winning record in that stretch is Pittsburgh at 4-2.

It might get ugly if the Browns reach the postseason, but Todd Monken's team has a better chance of getting there than the average fan might think.

articles.title: Bold Predictions for the Buffalo Bills' Post-Bye Stretch Run
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are locked in atop the AFC East at their bye week, with a critical Week 8 contest against the Baltimore Ravens on the post-break horizon.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are locked in atop the AFC East at their bye week, with a critical Week 8 contest against the Baltimore Ravens on the post-break horizon.

What should we expect from the AFC's Super Bowl favorite between now and Week 18?

Here are three bold predictions for what is sure to be an entertaining run toward the playoffs.

By Season's End, the Defense Will Be Above Average in Most Major Categories

Yes, it's been ugly. And yes, they have a lot of work to do. But I actually chalk up a large portion of Buffalo's defensive problems thus far to three dynamics that should give fans hope:

They're still adjusting to a brand-new defensive coordinator, and Jim Leonhard is still adjusting to them.

This is the youngest defense in the NFL.

Per ESPN's Power Index , they've faced the fifth-hardest schedule in the NFL thus far, but will face the ninth-easiest the rest of the way.

Each of those facts indicates there is room for growth and adaptation.

They aren't lacking raw skill. Are the off-ball linebackers low-ceiling starters? Sure. Are they devoid of current elite talent throughout the back seven? Absolutely. But the lion's share of the defensive issues thus far stem from this being a green unit trying to acclimate to a new scheme.

A lot of what has gone wrong is related to issues with communication and assignments, rather than an inability to make plays.

Leonhard and Joe Brady have exacerbated that challenge by varying personnel far too often for the defense to find any sort of groove. I understand the desire to give young backups like Kaleb Elarms-Orr and T.J. Parker reps, but 20 players are averaging more than 12 defensive snaps per game. That's overkill under the current circumstances, and injuries do little to explain it: The starting defenders have missed only nine combined games through six weeks.

On top of this, Leonhard seemingly has not become comfortable enough to get creative with schemes and disguises. What you see is what you get, and it's pretty limited in terms of blitzing and press coverage.

The result thus far is a 32nd-ranked defense with the second-worst EPA allowed per play in the NFL, albeit against a very tough schedule featuring established offenses and weapons like Nico Collins, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jahmyr Gibbs, Justin Herbert, Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua and Ashton Jeanty.

I mean, a staggering 33 percent of their snaps in pass defense this season have come against the reigning MVP and reigning MVP runner-up.

But you can see the potential. Rousseau is off to the best start of his career. He and Deone Walker look like legitimate All-Pro candidates. Bradley Chubb will eventually get his, and there's no shortage of depth up front. Christian Benford has already recovered from an ugly start as the top cover guy, while physical rookie Davison Igbinosun is improving quickly. He's already leapfrogged Maxwell Hairston, who wasn't cutting it as a starter but might now at least be the best No. 4 corner in the league.

Soon, the recently signed Tre'Davious White will be back in the mix as well. That's a pretty damn strong group of five corners.

Safety remains a concern considering the obvious C.J. Gardner-Johnson problem, but again, CJGJ and Cole Bishop do bring plenty of workable talent to the table as a duo.

With time, Leonhard and the coaching staff should be able to tap into that talent more effectively, especially as the stakes increase and they rely more heavily on their core players, who should cut down on communication breakdowns and blown coverages as Leonhard's first season wears on.

Last year, the run defense was the issue. This season, the Bills have fixed that problem. Now I expect a pass defense that ranked in the top 10 in EPA allowed per pass play last season to gradually return to respectability as players become more comfortable in the scheme and face a softer schedule down the stretch.

We'll See a Lot More of Ty Johnson and Ray Davis

It was obvious that James Cook actually changed his grip on the football in a Week 6 victory over the Raiders, which was necessary considering the veteran's four fumbles in the opening five weeks.

That said, it should be pointed out that Cook was going up against one of the worst run defenses in the NFL—a unit that to that point had surrendered an AFC-worst 5.2 yards per attempt on the ground—and that in this case, Cook actually averaged a season-low 4.3 yards per carry.

To be clear, it was still a solid overall performance featuring 153 scrimmage yards. But I couldn't help but notice that with the game on the line in the second half, Cook mustered just 33 yards on his final 11 rushes (3.0 per carry). And I can't help but wonder if he's shifting his focus to ball security at the expense of some productivity.

The fumbling issue is no fluke. It's a significant problem. The man has coughed up the ball nine times in his last 15 games, plus once in last year's playoffs.

Most fumbles in the last calendar year: 1. Cook (10) 2. Bijan Robinson (5) T-3. Aaron Jones (4) T-3. Cam Skattebo (4) T-3. Jonathan Taylor (4)

I believe Brady and offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael are going to eventually reduce Cook's workload, either because his fumbling habit bites them again, or because the specter of another fumble impacts his production and the staff's approach to backfield reps.

Ideally, it's more of the latter—a proactive attempt at preservation. And the offense might actually be better off that way in the long run, considering that the 27-year-old Cook has 989 touches since the start of 2023.

Besides, Johnson and Davis have earned it. Johnson averaged a stellar 4.5 yards per carry in his first three seasons as a Bill and has made a strong enough impact as a receiving weapon out of the backfield to keep defenses vulnerable when he takes handoffs. Davis averaged 4.7 yards per rush last year and has proven to be a tough back to take down, even if he's rarely going to pop off for an explosive play.

And critically, Johnson has just two fumbles on his last 226 touches, while Davis has yet to fumble on 206 career touches.

So while I expect that Cook will remain the top dog barring a true ball-security meltdown, I also think we'll see a lot more variation in the offensive backfield between now and January.

The Bills Secure the Top Seed in the AFC

My belief that the defense will recover and at least become more of an asset than a liability was likely a clue that I have this team not only returning to the throne in the AFC East, but also capturing the No. 1 seed in the conference for the first time this century.

It's time, and the path is actually somewhat clear. They don't own that top spot right now but actually control their own destiny for it because they'll host the thus-far-undefeated Chiefs on Thanksgiving.

Barring something catastrophic between now and then, the Bills will likely be favored in that matchup given their home-field and rest advantages against an aging Kansas City roster. That helps explain why sportsbooks give Buffalo and Kansas City similar odds to win the AFC despite the Chiefs' edge in the loss column.

Within the East, the Patriots had a historically soft schedule last year. But their remaining 2026 slate is actually much more challenging than Buffalo's, based on ESPN's Power Index.

Elsewhere, the 4-2 Broncos don't appear to be even a remote threat considering their glaring offensive struggles through six weeks. They rank 26th in terms of offensive EPA per play and will have their hands full just chasing down the Chiefs considering Kansas City's blowout Week 1 victory over Denver.

The AFC North's teams appear intent on cannibalizing one another. The Steelers lack firepower, the Ravens are facing a gauntlet the rest of the way, and we know better than to purchase Bengals stock.

The Jaguars are worth monitoring in the AFC South, but that Week 6 loss to the Texans in London was a killer for a team that plays just four more games in Jacksonville the rest of the season.

Meanwhile, Buffalo has the league's clear-cut MVP favorite in Josh Allen, who has positioned himself as the frontrunner for that award despite the fact his top receiver has been on the field for just 34 percent of the team's offensive snaps this season.

Now imagine Allen with a healthy DJ Moore and significantly more support from a settled-in Leonhard defense. Combine that with what we already know they can get from Cook and his backfield colleagues as well as a veteran offensive line, and the ingredients are all there.

Fans might find themselves frustrated by the fact the Bills have been winning ugly this season, but it's early. They're experiencing growing pains defensively and yet still find themselves at 5-1 at a perfectly timed bye.

Following a much-needed two-week stretch that should be used to both get healthy and iron out the kinks associated with substantial coaching changes, look for the Bills to hit their stride in November and December, culminating in another break via a first-round bye come January.

articles.title: Picking Each NFL Division Winner Entering the Heart of the 2026 Season
articles.summary: With Week 7 underway, all but about a dozen NFL teams remain within striking distance of the top spot in their division.
articles.body:
With Week 7 underway, all but about a dozen NFL teams remain within striking distance of the top spot in their division.

The Leader: Buffalo Bills (5-1) The Challenger: New England Patriots (4-3) Who'll Win It: Buffalo

The Bills have already lost to the Patriots, and they have not been winning pretty. New England could also benefit from being the host when the two meet again in December.

Still, the Pats' schedule is a lot tougher than last year's historically soft slate. With home games against the Raiders and Jets already complete, they're still two back of Buffalo in the loss column after falling to the Bears on Thursday night.

Keep in mind that the Bills have defeated the Patriots in December in each of the last six seasons (with four of those coming in Foxborough).

The Challengers: Cleveland Browns (4-2), Baltimore Ravens (4-2), Cincinnati Bengals (3-2)

I understand why Baltimore is the favorite, but the stars could be aligning for the Bengals.

The Bengals will have had two weeks to prepare for this weekend's game against the Ravens, and Lamar Jackson's availability and effectiveness following his ankle injury could be major factors.

A win could move the Bengals toward control of the division, especially given that they have the league's easiest remaining schedule, according to ESPN's Football Power Index .

I don't believe the Browns have the talent or experience to sustain what they've done over the first six weeks, and the Steelers don't have the firepower to win consistently.

The Bengals are flying under the radar with easily the best DVOA (defense-adjusted value over average) in the division. If they can stay healthy, I think this is their year.

The Leader: Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) The Challengers: Indianapolis Colts (2-4), Houston Texans (2-4) Who'll Win It: Jacksonville

The Colts are about to travel to Minnesota and Jacksonville. Based on their current trajectory, by the time they return to Indianapolis, they could essentially be four games back of the Jags.

This will realistically come down to Houston and Jacksonville, which is still a race thanks to the Texans' Week 6 win over the Jaguars in London. Still, the Jags are clearly the better team with the more talented quarterback, and both teams have equally forgiving schedules the rest of the way.

This will go down to the wire, but I trust Jacksonville a fair bit more right now. The team has the third-best DVOA in the league and a healthy cushion to work with en route to a second consecutive division title.

The Leader: Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) The Challengers: Denver Broncos (4-2), Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) Who'll Win It: Kansas City

I don't know that the Broncos have it in them this year. The offense has regressed significantly, and the sample is no longer small.

The Chiefs are averaging an AFC-best 6.7 yards per play with the conference's highest DVOA, while the Broncos are averaging an AFC-worst 4.4 yards per play with a middle-of-the-pack DVOA.

Now, Denver's schedule has been brutal while the Chiefs have yet to be strongly challenged, but Kansas City did crush the Broncos in the season opener and is well-positioned to lock up the tiebreaker when the two meet again in two weeks' time. The Broncos are winning ugly, and it doesn't strike me as sustainable now that the Chiefs are back in the picture after a one-year hiatus.

The Challengers: Dallas Cowboys (2-4), Philadelphia Eagles (2-4)

This is the ultimate "division by default" situation. The Eagles are imploding and have lost several key players, including quarterback Jalen Hurts, but the division-leading Giants are also in a quarterback quandary as they make the move to J.J. McCarthy—their third starter in a seven-week span.

I would have been tempted to include the Commanders in the conversation had they defeated San Francisco on Monday night to move to 2-3-1, but we're instead left with an unremarkable and unreliable Dallas team that can certainly still move the football and score points.

The Cowboys aren't trustworthy, but they've managed at least seven wins in nine of the last 10 completed seasons. They should reach that mark again as they navigate one of the league's easiest remaining schedules.

The Challengers: Chicago Bears (5-2), Green Bay Packers (4-2), Detroit Lions (3-2)

I'm surprised to see just how heavily favored the Vikings are, but a two-game cushion in the loss column is pretty significant in a division where the teams routinely cannibalize one another.

Minnesota already has victories over Green Bay and Chicago, and Kyler Murray is picking up steam while buoyed by the support of the top-ranked scoring defense in the NFL.

The Packers and Bears also face tougher slates the rest of the way, while the Lions' defense looks too problematic.

I won't completely rule out Chicago if Caleb Williams can keep building on things with Ben Johnson and that defense can keep making plays, but the margin for error is minuscule.

The Challengers: New Orleans Saints (2-4), Atlanta Falcons (2-4)

The Falcons are a legitimate challenger here—unlike the Saints, who look a year away—but Carolina's 34-3 blowout win in Atlanta in Week 2 tips the balance in the Panthers' favor.

That could leave the Falcons in a really tough spot even if they do charge back to make this interesting before the two meet again in Charlotte in Week 18.

Both offenses are strong, but the Panthers have more experience and established talent on defense, already hold a 1.5-game division lead and have a slightly easier remaining schedule.

The Challengers: Seattle Seahawks (3-3), Arizona Cardinals (2-4), Los Angeles Rams (2-4)

The Rams are listed as a challenger only because they entered the season as the overwhelming Super Bowl favorite, while the Cardinals are included because they're ahead of Los Angeles in the standings.

Neither can realistically overcome a four-game deficit here, especially with losses to San Francisco under their belts and L.A.'s injury situation.

It's also likely already too late for a Seattle team that has revealed some serious warts while losing three of four and now faces the NFC's most difficult remaining schedule.

The 49ers are hammering the rest of the league in DVOA, and there is a strong chance they will be 10-0 heading into their late-November showdown with a Seattle squad that could already be saddled with five losses.

articles.title: Biggest Risers and Fallers in 2027 NFL Draft Entering Week 8 of CFB Season
articles.summary: Every collegiate football program has reached the halfway point of its 2026 regular season. As expected, plenty of surprises have emerged along the way—both with the on-field product and continued development, or lack thereof, among future NFL prospects.
articles.body:
Every collegiate football program has reached the halfway point of its 2026 regular season. As expected, plenty of surprises have emerged along the way—both with the on-field product and continued development, or lack thereof, among future NFL prospects.

Next year's draft class has been particularly intriguing based on the potential of what it could be. However, early returns have not been as promising as expected, particularly at the game's most important position.

Those same expectations don't need to be lessened, though. They should be readjusted thanks to different names running with their opportunities. Meanwhile, some of the projections for highly regarded individuals should be revisited.

As a result, Bleacher Reports takes stock at the halfway point to see which prospects have impressed or disappointed the most.

Riser: QB Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State

A wait-and-see approach was necessary with Drew Mestemaker after transferring to Oklahoma State. He's answered the bell against Big 12 competition and emerged as the Bleacher Report Scouting Department's QB1.

Mestemaker became a known entity during the 2025 campaign when he led the nation with 4,379 passing yards. However, competition at North Texas is different than playing at Power Four program. Many wanted to see if the quarterback could thrive when facing tougher defenses on a regular basis.

To be fair, Mestemaker didn't need to learn a new offense since he followed North Texas head coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State. However, 92 new players entered the Cowboys program this year, which means the quarterback had plenty of work to do in building a rapport with his offensive teammates.

Initially, Mestemaker struggled, specifically in Week 1 against the Tulsa Golden Hurricane. The Okie State quarterback didn't look comfortable at all and couldn't help the Cowboys stave off the state rival. A week later, Mestemaker and Co. beat the Oregon Ducks.

During the subsequent four contests, the 20-year-old prospect completed 73 percent of his pass attempts. Mestemaker posted a 13-to-two touchdown-to-interception ratio during that stretch. He's also produced five straight games with 300 or more passing yards. Three of those contests came against conference rivals.

From an evaluation standpoint, Mestemaker displays top-notch arm talent, with the arm strength to drive the ball vertically and enough touch to layer passes. The 6'3", 215-pound gunslinger stands tall in the pocket and shows a willingness to stare down the gun barrel of an oncoming rusher. Plus, Mestemaker is a good athlete to help create chunk plays when forced outside of structure.

The redshirt sophomore can be arrogant with some throws, leading to turnovers. Also, he is only in his second season as a starting quarterback. So, his decision-making and how he sees the field still have room for improvement. But all of the physical traits are present to become the first quarterback off the board once April's draft begins.

Arch Manning has lived under tremendous scrutiny since being anointed as a 5-star high school recruit .

Entering this season, he was often projected as a future No. 1 overall NFL draft pick. Based on what he's shown so far this fall, the Texas Longhorns quarterback isn't currently worthy of first-round consideration and could use another year in college to refine the whole package.

There is a chaotic element to Manning's game, which makes his skill set much closer to his grandfather, Archie, than either of his Super Bowl-winning uncles.

Archie Manning was the second overall selection in the 1971 draft class, but he struggled greatly with the neophyte New Orleans Saints. Arch Manning has similar playmaking skills as an athlete working outside of structure and a lack of refinement to his overall game.

The latter is the major sticking point when evaluating Manning as a prospect for today's NFL, where teams are more willing than ever to develop quarterbacks with outstanding physical tools and tailor their offenses around them.

In the Texas quarterback's case, that same approach could be difficult for an NFL coaching staff, because his footwork and throwing mechanics are highly inconsistent, resulting in far too many poorly placed passes.

More importantly, Manning struggles to quickly work through his post-snap reads. He often predetermines where he wants to go with the ball, leading to dangerous throws, or takes too long getting through his options.

Peyton and Eli Manning both left college after their senior seasons. Arch Manning may need to follow the same path.

Notre Dame's Anthonie Knapp wasn't on the radar as a first-round talent entering the 2026 campaign, at least as an offensive tackle prospect.

His transition to guard has gone swimmingly, placing him among the 2027 class' top-12 prospects regardless of position and in competition with LSU's Jordan Seaton to become next year's highest-rated offensive line prospect.

Knapp took over Notre Dame's blind side as a true freshman. He spent his first two seasons as the Fighting Irish's left tackle. Typically, a collegiate blocker capable of manning the offensive line's most valuable position as a freshman doesn't move from that spot.

In Knapp's case, Notre Dame had another talented option in Will Black, who's a little longer and more naturally suited to the position.

Knapp told reporters this past spring that he had no qualms about transitioning to guard:

"I don't care. I'm a football player. I love football. I'm here to play football. I was a fourth-string center when I first got here, so it's whatever [offensive line coach Joe Rudolph] needs. He knows best. Whatever the team needs, whatever Coach needs. If they think I can be pretty good at guard, then I trust them. I'll do whatever it takes to be the best I can be and do what the coach says."

Along the interior, the 6'5", 305-pound lineman is a force physically. He plays with a certain level of violence at the point of attack that's not often seen from offensive tackle converts. Knapp fires out of his stance, generates movement and strains to finish blocks.

Now that everyone has seen what Knapp can do at guard, he's a Day 1 talent all day long, with no other interior option coming close to his level of performance so far this season.

Texas' Trevor Goosby entered the current draft cycle as the class' OT1 almost by default.

A year ago, the junior prospect showed impressive growth during his first season as a Longhorns starter. He was expected to continue along the same trajectory this fall. Instead, he's been surpassed by others, specifically LSU's Jordan Seaton.

Goosby's selling points are obvious. He has the requisite size (6'7", 325 lbs) and wingspan to be a starting NFL left tackle. The underclassman also displays the natural power and grip strength to displace and control defenders in the run game.

However, an offensive tackle's value is built upon a foundation of what the individual can do as a pass protector. Stiffness in Goosby's lower body has become evident. The first-team All-SEC honoree tends to play high, struggles to redirect and may not be able to handle NFL speed off the edge.

Despite those concerns, Goosby still has long-term starting potential. His subpar athletic profile simply caps his ceiling. As a result, Seaton quickly and easily surpassed Goosby as OT1 due to the LSU product's natural and smooth movement skills.

Now, Texas' left tackle looks far more like a Day 2 option alongside other prospects, like USC's Elijah Paige and Kentucky's Lance Heard, who have surged throughout this process. Overall, the offensive tackle class looks much stronger than it did prior to the start of the campaign, which further diminishes Goosby's standing.

A safety, Caleb Downs, carried the highest grade among the 2026 draft class. Texas' Jelani McDonald isn't in the same tier as Downs, but the previous example shows how valued a complete safety prospect can be.

Ultimately, Downs fell to the 11th overall pick during this past April's draft primarily due to positional value. Right now, McDonald has earned his status as B/R's No. 1 safety and a legitimate first-round talent.

"McDonald is exactly the kind of player the NFL needs today," B/R scout Daniel Harms tweeted . "He's a physical, 'A+' run defender, high-level communicator and has the instincts to take away routes over the middle of the field."

The senior prospect understands his angles, both when he's defending the run or playing in space. To Harms' point, McDonald posted the third-lowest missed tackle rate among qualifying safeties last season, according to CFB Film Room . He's been as good or better this fall. The defensive back is currently on pace to surpass last season's total of 80 tackles. McDonald's on-ball plays have decreased, but he still tends to be in the right spot to make life difficult on receivers.

While other Longhorns made this list after disappointing starts, McDonald deserves recognition for the complete player he is. His performance allowed him to surpass Notre Dame's Brauntae Johnson (injured) and Georgia's KJ Bolden as the incoming crop's top safety.

The Miami Hurricanes' defensive line was nearly unblockable a season ago. Defensive tackle Ahmad Moten was a big part of the unit's success, especially down the stretch, when he emerged as college football's best interior pass-rusher. He hasn't been quite the same this fall.

To be fair, Moten was slowed at the start of the season by an arm injury. He returned against the Clemson Tigers and looked like the explosive upfield defender everyone hoped to see this season. At times, some inconsistency can be found regarding his get-off and how he handles blocks at the point of attack.

An argument can be made that Moten is somewhat of a feast-or-famine defensive tackle prospect. He can certainly generate outstanding plays in the backfield, but he'll also get washed out of others due to playing with a high pad level and suspect anchor.

As this season progresses, more consistency, while staying healthy, will be key, because Moten was viewed as a potential first-round draft pick entering this season. With Miami at 6-0 and now ranked as the nation's No. 1 team, the spotlight will certainly shine brightly upon the Hurricanes' best players.

A second-half surge similar to last year's should propel Moten back toward his original projection. As of now, he stands as B/R's DL6 and sits outside of the scouting department's top 75 prospects.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson Talks Best NFL RB Debate, Falcons, Texas, Arch Manning and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons star Bijan Robinson is well aware of the ongoing debate over the best running back in the NFL.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons star Bijan Robinson is well aware of the ongoing debate over the best running back in the NFL.

However, even after Baltimore Ravens veteran Derrick Henry declared him "the best in the game right now" earlier this season, Robinson is focused on letting his game speak for itself.

"For me, I just gotta stay consistent in my play. Just keep being better every single game, keep being better than the last week that I played, and just gaining that confidence weekly, because, like you said, there's a lot of great running backs in this league, man, and they're doing a lot of great things for their team," Robinson told Bleacher Report. "So I gotta make sure that I'm doing everything that I can do to enhance this team, enhance the offense, and just continue to stay dangerous week to week, like those guys are on their teams."

"Those guys" include the likes of Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs, Kansas City Chiefs star Kenneth Walker III and Henry, who told reporters before a Week 5 matchup between the Ravens and Falcons that Robinson is "doing it all. I ain't going to shy away from it. He's doing a great job."

Entering Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers, Robinson is ranked second in the NFL with 641 rushing yards while adding four touchdowns on 111 carries. He's also produced 20 catches for 128 yards and a touchdown. He's tied with Walker for the league lead with seven explosive runs of 20 yards or more. The 24-year-old rose to the top of the "best running back" debate with 194-yard and 145-yard performances in back-to-back wins over the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints.

"I think God gave me a gift to do a lot of things on the field. My ability to make people miss, read the hole, hit the right angles, set up blocks and then just attack upfield and then be dangerous in the pass game as well. You can line me up anywhere on the field and be effective," Robinson said of what separates him from other ball-carriers. "So I think those are the things, even my pass protection, keeping the quarterback clean, and just the all-around game of what I bring to the table. I think that's what keeps elevating my game, and that's what I'm trying to continue to keep doing every single year that I play the game, is just to be effective in all aspects of the game."

Robinson, who was rewarded with a three-year contract extension worth up to $75 million with $51 million guaranteed this past offseason, said he also made a point to focus on taking on more of a leadership role entering his fourth year in the NFL. His effort paid off, as he was named a team captain for the first time in his career.

"Making sure I'm my best self on the field, and that the guys can hear my voice and trust that I'm saying the right things in the locker room, trust that I'm saying the right things when the game gets tough, when the game gets hard. Make sure that they can rely on me, not just on the field, but if I have something to say to them, or to the team, that it can bring everybody together," Robinson said of his mindset entering this year. "But I think that confidence in my leadership is the biggest thing that I've been working on this offseason, and I really appreciate the guys listening and hearing me if I do have something to say, because it's always positive and it's always just trying to help everybody in the locker room."

Robinson said he helped improve his self-confidence through his new partnership with Invisalign for its "SHIFT Happens" campaign, fulfilling the mantra "look good, play good."

"Obviously, confidence is a big thing for me. I take a lot of care of myself, so my smile and my oral health are very important to me. And I really wanted to take care of my teeth in a way of doing it without the wires or the brackets, just so I can have a confident smile on and off the field," Robinson said. "So that's why I chose the Invisalign Clear Aligners, because I can take care of myself and take care of my teeth and my smile, because I smile a lot. I'm a very positive guy.

"... As I be making people miss on the field, and smiling at my teammates or smiling at them, I don't want them to be like, 'You got some bad teeth,'" he added with a laugh. "So that's something I try to avoid. So for me, making sure that my confidence in my oral health is ready to go, so when I do go out there and play for God and just have a great game for Him and my teammates, and then when the interviews come after, I could be confident in that smile and making somebody else smile as well. That's why it's so important to me."

Despite entering Week 7 with a 2-4 record, the Falcons still have the NFC South crown in sight, as the Carolina Panthers lead the division at 3-2. Robinson admitted that Atlanta needs to increase its sense of urgency during this stretch against tough opponents.

"It's been a little bit of a roller coaster for us. You know, lost two, won two, and then lost these past two. So for us, I think it's really important to make sure we're doing all the little things right in the week to prepare for these games on Sundays," he said. "We gotta be able to start fast every single game, and I think that it starts at practice, like start fast at practice and make sure that we're all on the same accord when it comes to everything. But I think we've learned a lot in these past games. But now, for this portion of the season, we really have to understand what we have in front of us and take every game as a playoff game, man, because that's really what it is."

Robinson's alma mater, Texas, is also going through a rough patch, falling to No. 19 in the AP Top 25 after holding the No. 1 spot for four straight weeks earlier in the year. The former Longhorn suggested that head coach Steve Sarkisian will focus on the run game to open up the passing attack for struggling quarterback Arch Manning.

"I think we just need to come together on the offensive side of the ball and just get back to that bread and butter that Sark does, because we run the football at a high level and when he gets the running back going, then it opens up everything else for the pass game," Robinson said. "And I know that's what Sark's bread and butter is. And I know he's already talking to the guys like this is what we have to do in order to continue to win games throughout the season. And I think we have a tough four games coming up, but they're all winnable. I think the defense has been playing great, but the offense needs to help the defense. If they do that, then I think we'll be good for the remainder of the season."

Robinson also offered some wise words for Manning, who is facing questions as a top NFL draft prospect amid his recent downturn. The nephew of former NFL stars Peyton and Eli Manning has a lot of pressure to live up to expectations, but Robinson is confident that he'll be able to silence his doubters.

"I think the advice I do have for him is just to eliminate the external distractions, man. That's the biggest thing," Robinson said. "Keep everything in-house. Don't worry about social media. Don't worry about what people have to say, because his journey is his journey. And if he eliminates that, then I think he'll be his best self on the field and off the field, and everything else will take care of itself."

articles.title: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell emphasises commitment to more international games ahead of Saints-Steelers game in Paris
articles.summary: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said "everything is an option" when asked about expanding the NFL's international offering; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs and Super Bowl LXI
articles.body:
In layman's terms, the league has no plans to pump the brakes on its globe-trotting ventures amid a season in which a record nine international games will be played.

France enters the fold as one of three new territories for 2026 alongside Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro when New Orleans Saints face Pittsburgh Steelers at Stade de France on Sunday, live on Sky Sports NFL .

It is the newest extension to a format mirroring Formula 1's reach.

"It could lead to something else," Goodell told Sky Sports .

"Formula One actually helped me understand. I went to a race in Montreal and was looking at how they're racing, they race every week or two and have a lot of travel, a lot of ability, but also a lot of challenges. It's roughly 23 races, several of those already in the States.

"If we can get to 16 [international games] we're fairly close, it's the same number of markets we're reaching on a global basis.

"At some point we really have to think about it. Would we create an international franchise? Would we create a division? We want to think about that."

The NFL pushed its boundaries further than ever earlier this season by staging its first game in Australia as San Francisco 49ers beat Los Angeles Rams at the iconic MCG in front of 100,000 fans.

It had the feel of the league's boldest international move yet, though would also prove divisive amid players and coaches involved.

Goodell, though, says the league remains intent on establishing a long-term presence down under. Could the league possibly venture any further?

"We're looking! Everything's an option," joked Goodell of travelling as far as the moon.

"We were thrilled. When you look back at that, when you think about 10am on a Friday morning, 100,000 people coming to the NFL game, it was just remarkable.

"We shut down the town for most of the weekend. It was really, for us, an eye-opener to see something like that, so we were happy.

"We're looking back at it, too. When we play these games, we're thinking long-term. We're not coming into these games to play one game, we want to use it as a launchpad."

Goodell describes the NFL's global ambitions as a "360 challenge" as it continues to explore new markets, and credits the success of London as a host in paving the way for further expansion.

"London was the foundation, really," he said.

"The teams, what was really required, number one, was clearly to make it a successful event. One thing was to make sure the teams had an experience so they can go back and it hasn't completely disrupted their season, that in fact it enhances it.

"We were fortunate that in the first year we had the Giants and Dolphins and neither were playing great, but the Giants went on a run and what contributed to that was that they were here and they came together as a team."

Sunday's game in Paris arrives on the back of three straight in London across Tottenham and Wembley, while also preceding games in Madrid and Munich in November.

Mexico City returns to the schedule next month, while Asia has emerged as another potential destination.

articles.title: Week 7 Waiver-Wire Pickups and Sleepers Available in Majority of Fantasy Leagues
articles.summary: Week 7 got underway with Thursday night's showdown between the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears. As managers prepare for the remainder of the schedule, some will inevitably need to turn to the waiver wire for reinforcements.
articles.body:
Week 7 got underway with Thursday night's showdown between the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears. As managers prepare for the remainder of the schedule, some will inevitably need to turn to the waiver wire for reinforcements.

The Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders are also on bye this week.

While waiver claims have already been processed in most leagues, a few viable sleepers should still be available heading into the weekend. You'll find the top options for point-per-reception (PPR) leagues here, with picks based on recent production, projected roles, and individual matchups.

To be clear, there's a good amount of risk involved with New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who is rostered in only 13 percent of fantasy leagues. He rarely performed at an acceptable level during his time with the Minnesota Vikings, and he'll be on the road to face the Houston Texans.

However, McCarthy has been named the starter for Week 7 and moving forward, and he has the skills to operate as a dual-threat, not wholly unlike injured starter Jaxson Dart.

Though he only played a relief role in Week 6, McCarthy managed to tally 17.3 fantasy points.

Yes, there's a chance that McCarthy struggles with accuracy, decision-making, and ball security, as he often did in Minnesota. There's also a chance that he builds on last week's effort and shines against a Texans defense that has allowed the 10th-most fantasy points to opposing QBs.

Finding running backs on the waiver wire has been difficult in 2026, and it's been especially difficult late in the week. Managers who need to fill an RB slot in Week 7 should consider Cincinnati Bengals backup Samaje Perine.

Perine typically serves as a change-of-pace back behind starter Chase Brown. However, the Bengals experimented with giving Perine a heavier workload in Week 5—they were on bye last week—and got good results.

While Brown averaged a modest 3.0 yards per carry against the Miami Dolphins, Perine averaged 4.9. He also finished with a season-high 15.8 fantasy points.

Perine is a gamble this week. We don't know how Cincinnati's backfield split will look, and the Baltimore Ravens have been solid against the run. He appears to be trending upward out of the bye, though, and he's rostered in only nine percent of fantasy leagues.

New York Jets rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is still only rostered in 36 percent of leagues heading into the weekend, which is actually a bit surprising. The first-round pick out of Indiana was drafted to be the No. 2 receiver opposite Garrett Wilson, and he's looked the part when healthy.

Cooper had a 30-yard reception in Week 1 before suffering an ankle injury that landed him on injured reserve. He returned this past week and recorded six catches, 103 yards, one touchdown, and 19.3 fantasy points.

While Cooper doesn't have the juiciest Week 7 matchup, he has a tremendous amount of upside for the remainder of the season.

The Jets will host the Dolphins on Sunday, and while Miami has surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers, it's not because of a great defense. Teams simply haven't been pass-heavy against the Dolphins (4th fewest attempts against). Miami ranks 29th in net yards per pass attempt allowed.

Cooper should have a reasonable floor this week and a very high ceiling moving forward.

Things haven't gone well recently for Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks' passing attack. Things won't get any easier this week against a stout Kansas City Chiefs defense. Don't be surprised if the Seahawks turn to tight end AJ Barner to help get things moving.

The Chiefs have been susceptible to opposing tight ends this season, and Barner has been a reliable ancillary target behind Jaxson Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp. While he's 50 yards once this season, he's seen four or more targets in each of the past two games and has provided a passer rating of 100.0 when targeted.

Kansas City will undoubtedly focus on slowing Smith-Njigba, which could lead Darnold toward check-down options like Barner early and often.

The Chiefs have surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season. Barner is only rostered in 11 percent of fantasy leagues.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Jalen Hurts’ injury could be a blessing in disguise for the Eagles
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts’ health is the only thing that matters right now. The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback has been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral...
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts' health is the only thing that matters right now. The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback has been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, and the team expects him to make a full recovery. Still, his absence also leaves Philadelphia facing an uncomfortable reality: This season could be the opportunity the franchise needs to make a change at head coach.

The Eagles are 2-4, riding a four-game losing streak, and their offense has looked completely lost for stretches of the young season. The defense has its own problems, but the recurring offensive dysfunction is becoming impossible to ignore.

Nick Sirianni has delivered tremendous highs in Philadelphia, including a Super Bowl championship. However, the Eagles have repeatedly struggled to establish a consistent offensive identity. If Hurts' absence exposes those issues even further, ownership should use the offseason to move in a different direction.

The Offensive Coordinator Carousel Is Unsustainable

Sirianni's biggest problem might be the structure he has created around himself.

Philadelphia has cycled through offensive coordinators at an alarming rate. Shane Steichen left after the 2022 season to become the Indianapolis Colts' head coach. Brian Johnson followed, then Kellen Moore arrived and helped the Eagles win the Super Bowl before leaving to become the New Orleans Saints' head coach. Now Sean Mannion is tasked with getting the offense back on track.

Every new coordinator brings a different philosophy, terminology, and approach. Quarterbacks and receivers must adjust, the offensive line must learn new concepts, and the entire unit needs time to build chemistry.

That instability is especially damaging in an NFL increasingly defined by offensive innovation and continuity. Sirianni's supporters can point to the Super Bowl trophy and argue that his approach works. That's fair, but a successful head coach should build a structure that survives staff turnover, rather than repeatedly starting over whenever an assistant gets a better opportunity.

Sirianni also occupies an awkward middle ground. He delegates play-calling but remains heavily involved in shaping the offense. If the offense struggles, it's difficult to determine where the coordinator's responsibility ends, and the head coach's begins.

Philadelphia needs a clear offensive identity and a head coach who can establish it.

The Eagles shouldn't blow up their roster. They still have the foundation of a championship team.

Hurts remains their franchise quarterback. DeVonta Smith is an established playmaker, while Jalen Carter, Cooper DeJean, and Quinyon Mitchell give Philadelphia promising young talent to build around.

The problem isn't a lack of talent. It's whether the current coaching structure can consistently maximize it.

Philadelphia's recent collapses have been particularly concerning. The offense has struggled to score after halftime, and the losses to Chicago, Jacksonville, and Los Angeles exposed a team that too often looks incapable of adjusting when things go wrong.

Injuries have unquestionably played a role. Lane Johnson's retirement, Cam Jurgens' departure, injuries to Landon Dickerson and Saquon Barkley, and DeVonta Smith's absences have made life difficult. Hurts' diagnosis only adds to the adversity.

But injuries don't explain every schematic problem or every second-half collapse. And if the Eagles finish with a losing record, ownership will have to decide whether the current direction is worth another season.

Don't Let a Respectable Finish Cloud the Decision

The biggest danger for Philadelphia is finishing just well enough to avoid making a difficult decision.

Tanner McKee could keep the offense competitive. The defense could win games, and the NFC East could provide a path to the playoffs. If the Eagles scrape together a respectable finish, the pressure to retain Sirianni will grow.

But a few wins wouldn't erase the larger issues. Philadelphia needs to evaluate the season honestly, determine whether Sirianni is the right person to lead its next championship push, and make a decision based on the long-term outlook rather than the final win total.

If the answer is no, the offseason is the time to move on. A coaching change would give the Eagles an opportunity to hire an offensive-minded head coach with a clear vision, build continuity around Hurts, and use their draft capital to address an aging and increasingly injury-prone roster.

The Eagles don't need to start from scratch. They need to stop repeating the same cycle.

Jalen Hurts' injury is a serious setback, and nobody should pretend otherwise. But if this season finally forces Philadelphia to confront its coaching problem, the organization could emerge better positioned for the future.

The championship window isn't necessarily closed. It might simply be time for someone new to lead it.

articles.title: Steelers Get Good News on Alex Highsmith
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker Alex Highsmith (groin) is good to go for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints in […]
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker Alex Highsmith (groin) is good to go for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris. Highsmith does not have an injury designation after dealing with a groin issue, which limited him during the team's practices at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on Wednesday and Thursday.

Highsmith was an estimated full practice participant on Friday. The Steelers cancelled Friday's practice in Paris due to rain and wind in the forecast.

With three sacks, Highsmith currently ranks second on the team, behind only fellow outside linebacker T.J. Watt (4.5). Nick Herbig has posted two and cornerback Jalen Ramsey just as many, both coming in an overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last Sunday.

Highsmith also has 11 combined tackles and a pass defended on the season.

Some speculated after the Steelers extended Herbig's contract in the offseason that Highsmith might have been on the trade block. Highsmith talked during training camp about his future in Pittsburgh.

"I want to be a Steeler for life," Highsmith said. "I just want to go out there and do whatever I can to help bring another Super Bowl to this team, another Super Bowl to this city. I do want to be a Steeler for life. Just excited for this year, and obviously, our group. We're the best group in the league edge-wise. The three of us and Jack (Sawyer). Just really, really excited for the group that we have. I think there's going to be some special things."

articles.title: Former NFL player shares why he thinks Kenneth Walker ‘regression’ is going to start this week
articles.summary: Kenneth Walker has been in superb form during the first six weeks of the season, but Leger Douzable has suggested he is due for a regression, which could sta...
articles.body:
Kenneth Walker has been in superb form during the first six weeks of the season, but Leger Douzable has suggested he is due for a regression, which could start this week.

Walker joined the Kansas City Chiefs earlier in 2026 after helping the Seattle Seahawks secure the Super Bowl.

He now leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with his team 5-0 going into their Week 7 tie against the Seahawks.

But Douzable has suggested that Walker's 'regression' will start this week because Seattle have a defence which is 'tough' to run the football against.

Speaking via NFL on CBS, he said: "[Kenneth Walker] is due for a regression, which you would assume is going to happen because he's played at, at this pace, it's ridiculous, and I think it starts this week just because that is a tough defence to run the football against."

He added: "You don't think that Macdonald is going to know that the key focal point of the Kansas City offence is to minimise what Kenneth Walker III does. He's going to do everything in his power to make sure that Mahomes and that Chiefs offence is in second and third and long. That way their pass rushers can really get after the quarterback."

It remains to be seen if the Seahawks, who are 3-3 going into this game, have the ability to stop both Walker and Patrick Mahomes to put an end to the Chiefs' winning streak.

There is reportedly a belief within the NFL that the Denver Broncos may hold off on signing quarterback Bo Nix to a new contract this season or during the offseason if his play does not improve.

According to ESPN's Jeff Legwold , sources believe the most likely scenario if Nix doesn't play better will see the Broncos exercise the fifth-year option in his rookie contract next offseason, allowing the organization to take a "wait-and-see approach."

Regarding the state of Nix and head coach Sean Payton's offense, an anonymous, longtime NFL quarterbacks coach and play-caller told Legwold , "It's just hard to watch and hard for them to find something [Nix] or Sean can even dial up just to get their balance. … I don't think anybody saw that coming."

articles.title: New NFL Rumors Reveal Marvin Harrison Jr. 'Stopped Taking Calls' from Cardinals Coaches Before Trade
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr.'s relationship with the Arizona Cardinals coaching staff had reportedly deteriorated prior to his trade to the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
Marvin Harrison Jr.'s relationship with the Arizona Cardinals coaching staff had reportedly deteriorated prior to his trade to the Houston Texans.

ESPN's Josh Weinfuss reported Friday Harrison "stopped taking calls" from his coaches before he was dealt to the Texans for a pair of draft picks.

Harrison, the No. 4 pick in the 2024 draft, tallied just five catches for 85 yards on 13 targets in four games before the trade.

NFL legend announces Parkinson's diagnosis

One source told Weinfuss, "I just think at one point he was in his head, which made him play slower and cautious. His high expectations were a gift and a curse."

Weinfuss added the split between player and team dated back to Harrison's rookie season, when the Cardinals did not purchase Harrison a robotic quarterback the wide receiver had asked for. Harrison later purchased the machine himself, per Weinfuss.

The Cardinals' decision not to buy Harrison a Jugs machine was initially reported earlier this month by The Arizona Republic 's Theo Mackie . One source described the issue to Weinfuss as "not a good look for the team."

Harrison's exit took place amid the ascendance of Michael Wilson, who the Cardinals showed faith in as a top wideout by signing to a three-year, $75 million extension this offseason.

The Texans will hope to take advantage of the Cardinals' inability to develop Harrison into a WR1 by turning his career around in Houston, where the 24-year-old made three catches for 34 yards in his debut last Sunday.

Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said he expects Harrison's "workload to continue to increase" going forward, potentially starting Sunday with a Week 7 matchup against J.J. McCarthy and the visiting New York Giants.

articles.title: Lions Pegged as Trade Landing Spot for $111 Million DT
articles.summary: Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame named the Detroit Lions a potential fit for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne. The post Lions Pegged as...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions could really use an upgrade at cornerback at the NFL trade deadline. But that hasn't stopped pundits from linking the Lions to defensive playmakers at other positions.

This week, Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame called the Lions one of the two best potential fits for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne.

"Slated to hit free agency after this season, Payne is a fascinating player to watch. At 29, he hasn't had more than four sacks or 11 quarterback hits since 2022, the lone time he was a Pro Bowler," wrote Verderame. "Still, he's an impact player on the inside who commands double teams, logging at least 61% of the snaps every year of his career.

"If Washington makes Payne available, expect a market to develop."

Payne has 14 combined tackles, including two tackles for loss and five quarterback hits this season. He also has one sack and one forced fumble.

The veteran defensive lineman could be on the move before the deadline because the Commanders sit at 1-4-1 entering their bye this week. Payne has earned $111.8 million during his NFL career according to Spotrac .

Why Commanders DT Daron Payne Could Fit With Lions

The Lions enter Week 7 last in total defense and pass defense. They are also second-to-last in third-down percentage allowed and yet, the Lions are first in sacks.

Those statistics point to Detroit needing a cornerback. Based on the eye test, Lions fans everywhere would likely agree.

The team planned to have former first-round pick Terrion Arnold on the roster this season. They then didn't really replace him when the team released Arnold following his legal trouble over the summer.

Yet, some pundits are still proposing the Lions acquire a defensive lineman.

It's not the worst idea, especially if Detroit makes multiple trades before the deadline to improve the defense. Payne would add a veteran presence to the team's defensive line interior. That's something the Lions lost this past offseason with the departures of D.J. Reader and Roy Lopez .

Payne made the Pro Bowl in 2022 with a career-high 11.5 sacks, 18 tackles for loss and 20 quarterback hits. He also had five pass defenses that season.

Since then, the lineman has just 12 sacks in 55 games. But he remains a reliable contributor along the interior. If it doesn't take much draft capital, the Lions kicking the tires on acquiring Payne would make sense.

The question of whether the Lions could be in the market for someone like Payne greatly depends on how aggressive general manager Brad Holmes will be in the market. Being aggressive at the trade deadline isn't typical for Holmes.

Last season, the Lions didn't make any significant trade deadline acquisitions. The year prior, they added one player through a notable trade — edge rusher Za'Darius Smith .

If the Lions are only going to acquire one player again, it should be a cornerback. Payne is a nice to have, but he isn't essential to trying to fix the Detroit defense.

With Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams , the Lions have two quality starting defensive tackles. Dan Campbell has also regularly praised the team's interior defensive line depth such as rookie Skyler Gill-Howard .

The Lions have two and a half weeks to decide their trade deadline strategy. The league's trade deadline is set for Tuesday, November 10.

articles.title: NFL would cancel Paris game if unsafe due to riots, Steelers’ Rodgers says
articles.summary: Steelers to face New Orleans Saints in ⁠Saint-Denis on Sunday, about 10km from where Saturday’s protests are expected.
articles.body:
The NFL would have ‌cancelled its first regular-season game in Paris, scheduled for Sunday, if the situation were ⁠unsafe, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback ⁠Aaron Rodgers said, referring to the recent protests in the French capital.

France experienced some of its worst urban unrest in years last weekend, prompting President ⁠Emmanuel Macron to tighten curbs on protests on Thursday amid fears that demonstrations planned for Saturday could turn violent.

The Steelers face the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in ⁠Saint-Denis on Sunday, about 10km from Place de la Bastille, where Saturday’s protests are expected to begin.

Four-time NFL MVP Rodgers said he was confident the game would go ahead as planned.

“I definitely think that the NFL is alert to what’s going on,” he told a news conference on Friday.

“This game ‌means a lot to the NFL. If it was unsafe, then I’m sure we wouldn’t be here.”

The first NFL regular-season game in Paris has been largely overshadowed by the nationwide protests, with new demonstrations planned for Saturday. The Steelers informed fans on Thursday that a “Steelers House” fan event in the Bastille neighbourhood would not go ahead.

The US State Department issued a security alert on Thursday night, calling on its citizens to “avoid demonstrations and areas of unrest”.

“Americans in ⁠Paris for the NFL game on Sunday, October 25 should also ⁠exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings,” added the department.

But the unrest is not the only thing that has disrupted the build-up to the game, with Storm Austen hitting part of the country. Meteo France, the national ⁠weather agency, has issued orange alerts for much of the northwest, including the Paris region.

The Steelers landed in France on Friday morning and were due to practice at the Stade de France ⁠before holding a news conference.

They eventually cancelled their training session due to bad weather and the news conference was moved to their hotel in Paris.

The Saints have been practicing this week in Versailles after arriving in France on Monday.

“Due to elevated ‌wind and rain conditions, in accordance with local authorities, there will not be a media viewing portion during today’s Saints practice,” said a statement.

The NFL also cancelled a fan ‌event ‌on Friday.

“NFL Experience Paris presented by Wilson is closed for the rest of today due to adverse weather. Please do not attend the site,” the NFL said in a statement.

articles.title: Ian Rapoport shares encouraging update on Puka Nacua's calf injury
articles.summary: Ian Rapoport said that after Puka Nacua underwent testing on his injured calf, it's believed to be "more minor than anything else."
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was unable to finish practice on Thursday after suffering a calf injury, causing him to exit early. He's the latest Rams player to get hurt , joining a list that includes Davante Adams, Kobie Turner and Myles Garrett.

Fortunately, Nacua's injury isn't believed to be serious.

Ian Rapoport said on NFL Network Friday that Nacua underwent testing on his calf and it's believed to be "more minor than anything else." Rapoport stopped short of saying Nacua's removal from practice was "precautionary because it's not nothing," but Rapoport doesn't believe it's a "significant injury.

"Yesterday we learned that Puka Nacua left practice with a calf injury," he said. "Went to go have tests. My understanding is after the tests, it was more minor than anything else. I wouldn't say precautionary because it's not nothing, but at least not a significant injury. What that doesn't tell us is whether or not Puka Nacua will be able to play this weekend for the Los Angeles Rams. … I think it's safe to say Puka Nacua is up in the air for Sunday."

Nacua missed two games earlier this season with a hip/groin injury, which he also suffered in practice. It's unclear whether this calf injury will keep him out of Sunday's contest against the Las Vegas Raiders , especially considering how late in the week it occurred.

The Rams have one more practice on Friday before releasing their final injury report of the week. They will then have to make a final decision on his status 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday when inactives are due.

articles.title: Cairo Santos Lobbied Bears Coaches to Attempt Game-Sealing 58-Yard FG vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson's gutsy decision to let kicker Cairo Santos attempt a 58-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots was heavily influenced by Santos himself.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson's gutsy decision to let kicker Cairo Santos attempt a 58-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots was heavily influenced by Santos himself.

Santos told reporters after the game that he was vocal about wanting the opportunity to try the kick, saying, "I was talking to [special teams coordinator Richard Hightower] HT that I felt good about the line. And then Ben asked, 'Does he want it?' And I heard it and I told HT, 'I want it.' And then Ben said he wants it. I'm thankful that Ben trusts me on that."

NFL legend announces Parkinson's diagnosis

Johnson confirmed the pre-kick conversation, saying, "One, we felt good about being inside that line, and two, we asked him, he said, 'Absolutely, I need redemption because I missed one earlier.' He came through for us in a big way."

Santos missed a 53-yard field goal earlier in the fourth quarter, so when Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was sacked, pushing Chicago to the edge of field goal range, it seemed likely that Johnson would punt the ball back to New England.

Instead, Johnson put his trust in Santos, who nailed a new career long to extend the Chicago lead to nine with 1:34 remaining in the fourth quarter, essentially putting the game away.

After a Patriots field goal, the Bears recovered an onside kick, and clinched a 5-2 start to the season in the process.
